limitations: Evidence: the 12 laws of CLM-C05-17 without a model of order 2 have none of orders 6 and 10 (whether 1313 has a model of order 14 is undecided); spectra are closed under products, and a product reaches an order 2 (mod 4) only through a factor of order 2; all known linear models of these laws have odd order or order 4, 8, 16, .... No proof. The statement is false for laws of other shapes: 1719, x = (yy)((xx)y), has no model of order 2 but one of order 6 (EXP-C05-03). A possible approach is a parity (sign) argument on the translations, as for law 167 (Theorem 2).
statement: If a law of the form x = y*T(x, y) has no model of order 2, it has no finite model of any order n = 2 (mod 4).
title: H-C05-J: a law x = y*T without a model of order 2 has no model of any order n = 2 (mod 4)
